newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls confidence vote on dairy decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls confidence vote on dairy decree.

text.p: The Italian government on Monday called a confidence vote in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on a decree bill to reform the milk sector.

Giorgio Bogi, Minister for Relations with Parliament, announced the do-or-die measure in parliament. It relates to a package of reforms for the dairy sector, which has been hit by a bitter dispute with farmers over strict European Union quotas.

Parliamentary sources said the vote would start at 1030 GMT on Tuesday. The centre-left government, which relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, must resign if it loses but was not expected to face serious danger.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government unveiled the decree, containing emergency aid measures for the dairy sector, in January after farmers blockaded roads and airports for two weeks to protest against hefty EU overproduction fines.
The farmers had accused the state of failing to advise them of their correct quotas and initially refused to pay.

The government responded with the bill, which offered cheap loans and payments by instalment plus a pledge to set up a commission to examine the farmers' grievances. Italy has also asked the European Commission to increase its milk quotas.
Bogi said the confidence vote was called over a government amendment to the decree and includes changes to the text of the draft bill since adopted by parliament's agriculture commission.

The European Commission decided earlier this month to withhold farm funds from Italy, Spain and Greece for failing to pay the so-called EU super-levy fines for overshooting their strict 1995-96 milk output quotas.
Italian farmers were fined 192.2 million Ecus ($167 million). They have already made a partial payment.
Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto survived a no-confidence vote last month after opposition parties tried to oust him for his handling of the crisis.

Decree laws issued by the government have force for only 60 days unless approved within that time by parliament. They cannot be re-issued and Prodi has called several confidence votes to push through legislation. He has survived comfortably.
